title: Cofactor Matrix, Adjoint and Inverse
quickIdea: The adjoint is the transposed cofactor matrix; it exists for every square matrix and manufactures the inverse exactly when the determinant is not zero.
remember: adj(A) is the transpose of the cofactor matrix: adj(A)_ij = C_ji. The transpose is part of the definition, not an afterthought.
A adj(A) = adj(A) A = |A| I_n. When |A| = 0 this reads A adj(A) = O, so the adjoint still exists.
A^-1 = adj(A)/|A| exists exactly when |A| is not 0; the inverse is unique, (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1 and (A^T)^-1 = (A^-1)^T.
|adj A| = |A|^(n-1), adj(adj A) = |A|^(n-2) A, adj(AB) = adj(B) adj(A) and adj(kA) = k^(n-1) adj(A).
For 2 x 2: if A = [[a,b],[c,d]] then adj(A) = [[d,-b],[-c,a]] and A^-1 = adj(A)/(ad - bc).
An orthogonal matrix is its own adjoint up to sign: adj(A) = det(A) A^T when A is orthogonal.

example.prompt: A = [[3,1],[2,4]]. Find adj(A), verify A adj(A) = |A| I, and write A^-1.

gateAngle: GATE prefers the identities |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) and A adj(A) = |A| I to a full inverse computation. The only inverse question found in this topic, GATE CSE 1994 Q.3.12, is descriptive and is recorded as a gap rather than forced into the MCQ schema.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A is 3 x 3 with |A| = 2. Find |adj(A)| and |adj(adj A)|.
variations.why: |adj A| = |A|^(n-1) = 2^2 = 4, and applying the same rule twice gives |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n-1)^2) = 2^4.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why is adj(A) defined even when A is singular?
variations.answer: Because it is built from cofactors, which are determinants of (n-1) x (n-1) submatrices and always exist; only the step A^-1 = adj(A)/|A| needs |A| to be non-zero.
variations.why: The adjoint is a matrix of numbers; the inverse is the adjoint divided by a number that may be zero.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A is 2 x 2 with adj(A) = [[2,3],[4,5]]. What is A?

trap.what: Forgetting to transpose the cofactor matrix, or writing |adj A| = |A|.
trap.why: adj(A) is the transposed cofactor matrix, and each of the n cofactors carries one factor of |A|, so the determinant of the adjoint is |A|^(n-1).
trap.counterexample: For A = [[3,1],[2,4]] the cofactor matrix is [[4,-2],[-1,3]] but adj(A) = [[4,-1],[-2,3]]; and for a 3 x 3 with |A| = 3, |adj A| = 9, not 3.

check.question: A is 3 x 3 with |A| = 5. What is |A adj(A)|?
check.explanation: A adj(A) = |A| I_3 = 5 I_3, and the determinant of 5 I_3 is 5^3 = 125.
